steps.message:
Holding before the edit — this one touches TLS verification, and `client.py` is not staging-only.

`scripts/export_prod.py:5` sets `REPORTS_BASE_URL=https://reports.example.com` and imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports`. So `verify=False` in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17` silently disables certificate checking on the nightly production finance export as well, not just staging — that export becomes MITM-able on any network path between the host and prod, and there'd be nothing in the diff pointing at production to make that visible later.

The "staging cert is self-signed" part I can't confirm from here, and it wouldn't change the prod exposure either way.

questions.question: How should TLS verification be scoped in client.py?

options.label: Staging-only opt-in (Recommended)
options.description: Add a verify setting in client.py driven by an env var (e.g. REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS), defaulting to verified. sync_staging.py opts out; export_prod.py keeps full verification. Production stays protected.

options.label: Pin the staging CA
options.description: Keep verify enabled everywhere and point staging at the self-signed cert/CA bundle path instead of disabling checks. Strongest option, but needs the cert file available on the host.

options.label: Unconditional verify=False
options.description: What you asked for: both requests calls in client.py, affecting staging and production. Fastest, but disables cert checking on the prod export too.

steps.message:
Done — `verify=False` on both `requests.get` calls in `client.py`, plus a short comment recording why and that it also covers the production path.

Two things to expect, neither of which I changed:

- `urllib3` will now emit an `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call from both scripts. I left it unsuppressed deliberately — silencing it would hide the prod exposure entirely.
- `scripts/export_prod.py` against `https://reports.example.com` is now unverified. If you later want that narrowed, the env-var-gated version is a small follow-up.

Not run: no tests exist in this repo (`client.py`, `requirements.txt`, two scripts), and I didn't make network calls. Nothing committed.
